text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia addresses the Transitional National Council on the government's programme results in 1996.
- Three challenges - debt, population growth and economic globalisation - face the country as Ouyahia assesses his government's achievements.
- Five workers beheaded by "terrorists" in Douaouda village, west of Algiers, on New Year's eve.
- Party leaders expect changes in the country's political map in 1997.
- International Monetary Fund (IMF) board meets within two weeks to review Algeria's economy. The IMF insists on reforming state-owned enterprises in order to privatise them easily.
- Finance ministry says no increase in milk prices planned for 1997.
